docs.title: Recent advances in Alzheimer's disease: From molecular mechanisms to therapeutic strategies
docs.text: Source: Cell, Leading Edge Review (2026) Authors: Michelle D. Rudman, Jason D. Ulrich, David M. Holtzman DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2026.06.006 Institution: Washington University, Department of Neurology

docs.title: TL;DR
docs.text: First disease-modifying therapies for Alzheimer's disease (AD) now exist — lecanemab and donanemab slow cognitive decline by ~30% over 18 months through amyloid-β removal. However, cognitive decline persists after amyloid clearance due to co-pathologies (tau, neuroinflammation, lipid dyshomeostasis) that become semi-autonomous. Major advances include: structural elucidation of disease-specific amyloid and tau filaments via cryo-EM, discovery of APOE protective variants, recognition of adaptive immune system contributions, and emergence of plasma biomarkers (p-tau217, p-tau181, GFAP) enabling earlier diagnosis.

docs.title: Amyloid-β (Aβ)
docs.text:
• Production: Cleavage of APP by β-secretase (BACE1) and γ-secretase, regulated by synaptic activity and SORL1^[raw/articles/recent-advances-alzheimers-disease-cell-review-2026.md]
  • Timeline: Aβ accumulation begins ~20 years before cognitive impairment^[raw/articles/recent-advances-alzheimers-disease-cell-review-2026.md]
  • Structural heterogeneity: Cryo-EM revealed disease-specific Aβ42 filaments distinct between sporadic and familial AD, and different from synthetically derived fibrils^[raw/articles/recent-advances-alzheimers-disease-cell-review-2026.md]
  • Pathogenic species: Evidence supports Aβ protofibrils (lecanemab) and mature plaques containing pE3-Aβ (donanemab) as most pathogenic; antibodies targeting monomers failed^[raw/articles/recent-advances-alzheimers-disease-cell-review-2026.md]

docs.title: Tau
docs.text:
• Hyperphosphorylation: Impairs microtubule binding, leads to misfolding, aggregation into filaments and neurofibrillary tangles^[raw/articles/recent-advances-alzheimers-disease-cell-review-2026.md]
  • Structural specificity: Cryo-EM structures of AD tau filaments identical to PART but distinct from CTE, Pick's, CBD, PSP^[raw/articles/recent-advances-alzheimers-disease-cell-review-2026.md]
  • Post-translational modifications: >95 distinct modifications across 88 residues; specific patterns correlate with disease stage and patient heterogeneity^[raw/articles/recent-advances-alzheimers-disease-cell-review-2026.md]
  • Propagation: Spreads trans-synaptically from entorhinal cortex → hippocampus → neocortex; involves cell-autonomous and non-cell-autonomous mechanisms (glial cells, extracellular vesicles)^[raw/articles/recent-advances-alzheimers-disease-cell-review-2026.md]

docs.title: Anti-Amyloid Antibodies
docs.text:
• Lecanemab (CLARITY-AD): 30% slowing of cognitive decline over 18 months; targets Aβ protofibrils; Fc-mediated microglial activation required^[raw/articles/recent-advances-alzheimers-disease-cell-review-2026.md]
  • Donanemab (TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2): Similar clinical benefit; targets N-terminal pyroglutamate Aβ (pE3-Aβ)^[raw/articles/recent-advances-alzheimers-disease-cell-review-2026.md]
  • Mechanism: Rapid amyloid removal slows tau pathology progression and attenuates neuroinflammation (dose-dependent effects)^[raw/articles/recent-advances-alzheimers-disease-cell-review-2026.md]
  • Limitations: Modest slowing relative to amyloid clearance; co-pathologies persist after amyloid removal; earlier intervention shows greater benefit^[raw/articles/recent-advances-alzheimers-disease-cell-review-2026.md]

docs.title: Other Therapeutic Approaches
docs.text:
• Anti-tau antibodies: Multiple candidates in trials (semorinemab, gosuranemab, etalanetug); mixed results so far^[raw/articles/recent-advances-alzheimers-disease-cell-review-2026.md]
  • Targeted protein degradation: PROTACs and AUTOTACs show efficacy in reducing tau accumulation; tau-targeting RING fusion proteins promote selective degradation of aggregated tau^[raw/articles/recent-advances-alzheimers-disease-cell-review-2026.md]
  • Gene therapy: AAVrh.10 delivery of APOE2-Christchurch variant suppresses amyloid and tau pathology in mice^[raw/articles/recent-advances-alzheimers-disease-cell-review-2026.md]
  • CAR-based therapies: CAR macrophages, CAR-T cells, and CAR astrocytes targeting amyloid in preclinical development^[raw/articles/recent-advances-alzheimers-disease-cell-review-2026.md]

docs.title: APOE Biology
docs.text:
• Rare protective variants: Discovery of APOE variants associated with reduced AD risk has led to breakthroughs in understanding APOE's role in modulating AD risk^[raw/articles/recent-advances-alzheimers-disease-cell-review-2026.md]
  • Therapeutic targeting: APOE2-Christchurch variant gene therapy shows promise in suppressing amyloid and tau pathology^[raw/articles/recent-advances-alzheimers-disease-cell-review-2026.md]

docs.title: Neuroimmunology
docs.text:
• Innate immune system: Microglial activation and phagocytosis required for anti-amyloid antibody efficacy; TREM2 signaling implicated^[raw/articles/recent-advances-alzheimers-disease-cell-review-2026.md]
  • Adaptive immune system: Recognition of its importance in neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration in AD; immunomodulatory approaches under investigation^[raw/articles/recent-advances-alzheimers-disease-cell-review-2026.md]
  • Biomarkers: GFAP, TSPO (microglia), sTREM2 reflect neuroinflammatory activity along AD continuum^[raw/articles/recent-advances-alzheimers-disease-cell-review-2026.md]

docs.title: Biomarker Discovery
docs.text:
• Fluid biomarkers: Plasma p-tau217 and p-tau181 track earliest amyloid deposition; p-tau205 correlates with later stages (brain atrophy, hypometabolism)^[raw/articles/recent-advances-alzheimers-disease-cell-review-2026.md]
  • Plasma brain-derived tau: Novel biomarker for AD-type neurodegeneration^[raw/articles/recent-advances-alzheimers-disease-cell-review-2026.md]
  • Neuroinflammation markers: Plasma GFAP, sTREM2; PET imaging with TSPO, MAO-B tracers^[raw/articles/recent-advances-alzheimers-disease-cell-review-2026.md]
  • Early detection: Plasma biomarkers enable identification of pathology in cognitively normal adults at risk^[raw/articles/recent-advances-alzheimers-disease-cell-review-2026.md]

docs.title: Entities
docs.text:
• Michelle D. Rudman: Researcher, Washington University, Department of Neurology^[raw/articles/recent-advances-alzheimers-disease-cell-review-2026.md]
  • Jason D. Ulrich: Researcher, Washington University, Department of Neurology^[raw/articles/recent-advances-alzheimers-disease-cell-review-2026.md]
  • David M. Holtzman: Senior author, Washington University, Department of Neurology; leading AD researcher^[raw/articles/recent-advances-alzheimers-disease-cell-review-2026.md]
  • Washington University: Knight Alzheimer's Disease Research Center^[raw/articles/recent-advances-alzheimers-disease-cell-review-2026.md]

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text:
• amyloid-beta: Primary constituent of neuritic plaques; Aβ42 more aggregation-prone; protofibrils and pE3-Aβ are pathogenic^[raw/articles/recent-advances-alzheimers-disease-cell-review-2026.md]
  • tau-pathology: Hyperphosphorylated tau aggregates into NFT; structural heterogeneity across tauopathies; correlates with cognitive decline^[raw/articles/recent-advances-alzheimers-disease-cell-review-2026.md]
  • neuroinflammation: Microglial and astrocyte activation; TSPO, GFAP, sTREM2 as biomarkers; both innate and adaptive immune involvement^[raw/articles/recent-advances-alzheimers-disease-cell-review-2026.md]
  • apoe: Major genetic risk factor; rare protective variants discovered; therapeutic targeting via gene therapy^[raw/articles/recent-advances-alzheimers-disease-cell-review-2026.md]

docs.title: Takeaways
docs.text:
1. Paradigm shift: 2023 marked first clear evidence that removing amyloid from brain can slow AD progression, validating amyloid hypothesis after decades of failures^[raw/articles/recent-advances-alzheimers-disease-cell-review-2026.md]

  2. Structural biology breakthroughs: Cryo-EM revealed disease-specific amyloid and tau filament structures, explaining clinical heterogeneity and enabling more targeted therapeutics^[raw/articles/recent-advances-alzheimers-disease-cell-review-2026.md]

  3. Early intervention critical: Earlier treatment (before extensive co-pathology develops) yields greater benefit, highlighting need for better early detection via plasma biomarkers^[raw/articles/recent-advances-alzheimers-disease-cell-review-2026.md]

  4. Multi-target approach needed: Amyloid removal alone insufficient; need complementary therapies targeting tau, neuroinflammation, and lipid dyshomeostasis^[raw/articles/recent-advances-alzheimers-disease-cell-review-2026.md]

  5. APOE insights pivotal: Discovery of protective APOE variants transformed understanding of AD risk and opened new therapeutic avenues^[raw/articles/recent-advances-alzheimers-disease-cell-review-2026.md]

  6. Biomarker revolution: Plasma biomarkers (p-tau217, GFAP, sTREM2) enable accessible early detection and disease monitoring^[raw/articles/recent-advances-alzheimers-disease-cell-review-2026.md]

  7. Immune system recognition: Both innate and adaptive immunity contribute to AD pathogenesis, expanding therapeutic possibilities beyond amyloid and tau^[raw/articles/recent-advances-alzheimers-disease-cell-review-2026.md]

  8. Hope for prevention: Preclinical trials (AHEAD 3-45, TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 3) testing prevention in asymptomatic at-risk individuals^[raw/articles/recent-advances-alzheimers-disease-cell-review-2026.md]

docs.title: TL;DR
docs.text: This Bowtie Insurance video exposes common myths about savings insurance products in Hong Kong. Key findings: only 6 out of 135 analyzed policies met their projected returns, "guaranteed principal" is often an illusion, and many policyholders receive significantly lower dividends than expected during sales presentations.^[raw/videos/savings-insurance-hong-kong-myths-bowtie.md]

docs.title: The "Guaranteed Principal" Illusion
docs.text:
• Savings insurance is marketed as "保本" (guaranteed principal protection)
  • This is often a marketing myth rather than actual protection of capital
  • Customers may not understand the conditions and scenarios where principal is not protected^[raw/videos/savings-insurance-hong-kong-myths-bowtie.md]

docs.title: Return Discrepancy Problem
docs.text:
• Actual dividend returns often fall short of "expected returns" shown by agents
  • Sales projections use optimistic assumptions that may not materialize
  • Customers experience disappointment when actual performance diverges from projections^[raw/videos/savings-insurance-hong-kong-myths-bowtie.md]

docs.title: Industry Performance Statistics
docs.text:
• Critical finding: Only 6 out of 135 savings policies analyzed met their projected return targets
  • This suggests 95.5% of analyzed policies underperformed relative to sales projections
  • Systemic issue in the industry, not isolated incidents^[raw/videos/savings-insurance-hong-kong-myths-bowtie.md]

docs.title: Surrender Value Risks
docs.text:
• "供斷保險" (stopping payments or surrendering) often results in significant losses
  • The video questions whether you can actually get your money back while retaining coverage
  • Long-term lock-up periods create opportunity costs and liquidity risks^[raw/videos/savings-insurance-hong-kong-myths-bowtie.md]

docs.title: Financial Health Risks
docs.text:
• Expensive savings plans can lead to insufficient actual life insurance coverage
  • Cash flow gets "hostaged" for decades
  • Policyholders may lack adequate protection for actual insurance needs due to high premiums going toward savings component^[raw/videos/savings-insurance-hong-kong-myths-bowtie.md]

docs.title: Notable Quotes
docs.text:
"踢爆 儲蓄保 保本 假象!!" - Exposing the illusion of guaranteed principal in savings insurance

"保險 Agent 未必想你睇的一條片…" - This video may show what insurance agents don't want customers to see

"供斷保險 = 拎番錢 又有保障？" - Surrendering insurance equals getting money back AND having coverage? (Questioning this claim)

docs.title: Entities
docs.text: • Bowtie Insurance 保泰人壽 - Hong Kong-based insurance company producing educational content^[raw/videos/savings-insurance-hong-kong-myths-bowtie.md]

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text:
• Savings Insurance (儲蓄保) - Insurance products combining protection and investment components
  • Term Life Insurance (純人壽) - Pure life insurance without savings/investment component, suggested as alternative
  • Dividend Realization Rate - Ratio of actual dividends received to projected dividends

docs.title: For Consumers
docs.text:
1. Be skeptical of sales projections - Expected returns are not guarantees
  2. Read policy documents carefully - Understand terms, conditions, and surrender values
  3. Separate insurance from investment - Consider term life insurance + separate investment vehicles for better transparency and control
  4. Understand lock-up periods - Long-term commitments create liquidity risks and opportunity costs
  5. Verify claims - Ask for historical performance data, not just projections

docs.title: For Financial Planning
docs.text:
• Savings insurance may underperform relative to alternative investment strategies
  • Prioritize adequate insurance coverage first, then consider investments separately
  • Consider the opportunity cost of locked-up capital in savings plans
  • Compare actual historical returns vs. projected returns before committing

docs.title: A shared neural basis underlying psychiatric comorbidity
Source
docs.text: Field Value Type article URL https://doi.org/10.1038/s41591-023-02317-4 Author Chao Xie, Shitong Xiang, Chun Shen, Xuerui Peng, et al. Published Nature Medicine, Volume 29, May 2023 Ingested 2025-01-21

docs.title: TL;DR
docs.text: Researchers identified a neuropsychopathological (NP) factor — a reproducible neural signature that underlies both externalizing (ADHD, ASD, ODD, CD) and internalizing (depression, GAD, ED, SP) symptoms. This NP factor represents delayed development of prefrontal circuits, leading to poor executive function, and generalizes across development, imaging modalities, and clinical populations.

docs.title: Key Points
docs.text:
1. NP Factor Identification: Using multitask fMRI connectomes from 1,750 adolescents (IMAGEN cohort), researchers extracted shared neural edges across 8 psychiatric symptoms (4 externalizing, 4 internalizing), revealing a crossdisorder neural factor.

  2. Neural Circuits: The NP factor primarily involves three networks — sensorimotor network (SMF), salience network (SAL), and frontoparietal network (FPN) — with key regions including ventral precuneus, medial prefrontal cortex, and inferior frontal gyrus.

  3. Neurobehavioral Correlates: Higher NP factor scores (indicating weaker connectivity) are associated with poor executive function — lower IQ, reduced working memory, and impaired risk adjustment — but not with non-executive cognitive domains.

  4. Genetic Basis: The NP factor is genetically associated with polygenic risk scores for ADHD and depression, and gene ontology analysis shows enrichment for neurodevelopmental processes (neuronal differentiation, axon guidance, synapse formation).

  5. Developmental Trajectory: NP factor scores decrease with age, indicating normalization during development. Higher scores at age 14 predict slower symptom reduction from adolescence to young adulthood.

  6. Generalizability: The NP factor is reproducible across multiple developmental periods (ages 10-29), generalizable to resting-state connectomes, and validates in clinical samples (ADHD-200, STRATIFY/ESTRA covering AN, BN, AUD, MDD).

docs.title: Notable Quotes
docs.text:
"We demonstrate that this NP factor might represent a unified, genetically determined, delayed development of the prefrontal cortex that further leads to poor executive function."

"The NP factor primarily involved three networks: SMF, SAL and FPN. These networks are critical for executive function, cognitive control and salience processing."

"Adolescence is a critical period for the maturation of these networks and that delayed development of prefrontal circuits may contribute to psychopathology."

docs.title: Background and Problem
docs.text: Psychiatric comorbidity — coexistence of multiple psychiatric conditions — affects 27.9% of adolescents aged 14-17. Individuals with comorbid diagnoses experience poorer outcomes and severe cognitive deficits. Traditional approaches treated comorbidity as a confounding factor to be removed, but recent evidence suggests shared neurobiological origins across disorders.

docs.title: The NP Factor
docs.text:
Using connectome-based predictive modeling (CPM) on multitask fMRI (stop-signal task for response inhibition, monetary incentive delay for reward processing, emotional face task for emotion reactivity), researchers built symptom-specific brain signatures for 8 disorders. Shared edges across all symptoms formed the NP factor.

Reliability: Test-retest reliability across 11 training-validation folds was ICC = 0.94 (excellent).

Longitudinal Stability: NP factor scores at age 19 correlated with scores at age 14 (r = 0.57), demonstrating temporal stability.

docs.title: Neural Architecture
docs.text:
Positive edges (associated with higher symptoms): Weaker FC within SMF, SAL, and FPN networks. Reduced connectivity correlates with symptom severity.

Negative edges (associated with lower symptoms): Stronger FC between these networks and other brain regions. Enhanced connectivity is protective.

Key regions: Ventral precuneus (self-referential processing), medial prefrontal cortex (emotion regulation, decision-making), inferior frontal gyrus (response inhibition, cognitive control).

docs.title: Neurobehavioral Characterization
docs.text:
Cognitive Domain Correlation with NP Factor P-value IQ -0.18 < 0.001 Working memory -0.15 < 0.001 Risk adjustment -0.12 < 0.001 Processing speed NS NS Memory consolidation NS NS

Conclusion: The NP factor is specifically associated with executive function deficits, not general cognitive impairment.

docs.title: Genetic Characterization
docs.text:
• ADHD PRS: r = -0.10, P = 0.002
  • Depression PRS: r = -0.09, P = 0.004
  • Gene ontology: Enrichment for neurodevelopmental processes (P < 0.001)
  • No enrichment for immune or metabolic pathways

docs.title: Generalizability
docs.text:
Developmental: Predicts symptoms across ages 10-29 in ABCD, IMAGEN, and HCP cohorts (r = 0.15-0.35, P < 0.01).

Modality: Resting-state NP factor predicts externalizing (r = 0.22) and internalizing (r = 0.18) symptoms.

Clinical samples: - ADHD-200 (N = 520): Predicts ADHD symptom severity (r = 0.28) - STRATIFY/ESTRA (N = 413): Predicts symptoms across AN, BN, AUD, MDD (r = 0.19-0.26)

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
1. IMAGEN cohort is primarily European ancestry (population-based, limited diversity)
  2. Clinical samples had smaller sizes and different age ranges
  3. Limited cognitive assessment (executive function, processing speed, memory only)
  4. Environmental factors not examined (genetic-only focus)

  • — FC, temporal correlation between brain regions
  • prefrontal-cortex-development — Maturation of executive circuits during adolescence
  • — Cognitive control processes (working memory, inhibition, decision-making)

docs.title: My Takeaways
docs.text:
This study bridges internalizing-externalizing divide by identifying shared neural circuits. The NP factor represents a mechanistic link between genetic risk, brain development, and cognitive dysfunction. Most importantly, adolescence emerges as a critical window — connectivity patterns normalize during development, but delayed maturation predicts chronic symptoms. This suggests early intervention targeting prefrontal circuits during adolescence could prevent chronic psychopathology.

The methodological strength is impressive: 11-fold cross-validation for reliability, longitudinal testing for stability, and validation across 3 cohorts, 2 modalities, and 2 clinical samples. The limitation is the homogeneity of the IMAGEN cohort (European ancestry), limiting generalizability to other populations.

The NP factor's specificity to executive function (not all cognition) is clinically meaningful: it suggests interventions should target executive control rather than broad cognitive enhancement.

docs.title: Terminal Boredom and Endstage Screen Addiction (YouTube, ~46:00)
docs.text: Creator: Dr K (Healthy Gamer) Date: Not specified in transcript Duration: ~46:00 Video ID: OwlXbUYDf0w URL: Terminal Boredom and Endstage Screen Addiction

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Dr K explains "terminal boredom" — an endstage manifestation of screen addiction where people become so intensely bored they literally cannot do anything. The video covers dopamine tolerance mechanisms, executive function atrophy, impulse control deterioration, and the arms race between platforms to activate more brain circuits.

docs.title: 1. Endstage vs Early Stage Addiction
docs.text:
Early stage (alcohol example): - Cravings - Withdrawal symptoms (shakes) - Clear problem: "I can't put this down"

Endstage: - Affects multiple organ systems - Liver cirrhosis, heart damage - Therapist trained in addiction may not know about liver damage

Endstage screen addiction (new phenomenon): - Manifests as "terminal boredom" — people so bored they can't do anything - Lack of willpower, no direction, can't focus, "everyone has ADHD now" - These are manifestations of years of screen addiction, not separate problems

docs.title: 2. Dopamine Tolerance: Receptor Downregulation
docs.text:
The mechanism: - Normal: 3 receptors, 3 dopamine molecules → 3x pleasure - Screens increase dopamine (6x signal) - Brain protects itself by eliminating receptors (down to 2) - Same 6x release now produces only 4x response - Increase stimulation to 9x → back to 6x - Brain eliminates another receptor (down to 1) - Endstate: Very few receptors, minimal response

Tolerance is universal: Same mechanism as alcohol, marijuana, nicotine tolerance

docs.title: 3. Four Stages of Addiction
docs.text:
Stage Manifestation What's Happening Stage 1 Games/content are fun Normal receptor count, normal pleasure Stage 2 Games/content are less fun Receptors eliminated, tolerance developed Stage 3 Other things are less fun Further receptor loss; only screens work Stage 4 Terminal boredom Very few receptors; even screens don't work

Dr K's observation: 5 years ago, patients said "things aren't very fun." Now they say "I can't do anything."

docs.title: 4. Real-World Progression: The Toilet-to-Chair Example
docs.text:
Early stage: - "I want to play a game" - Takes screen to toilet - Plays while using toilet

Advanced stage: - Moves toilet next to chair - Replaces chair with toilet - "Can play in a degenerate way way longer than any other normal human"

Illustrates complete reorganization of life around screens.

docs.title: 5. Timeline
docs.text:
• 2007: Smartphone invented
  • 2012-2014: First 5-7 years — initial manifestations
  • 2017-2019: Additional 5 years — endstage appears
  • 2024+: Terminal boredom increasingly visible in clinical practice

docs.title: 6. Executive Function Rust
docs.text:
The human body rusts if you don't use it — it doesn't wear out.

Executive function: Planning and executing tasks - Takes abstract issue ("move out of house") - Breaks into pieces (find apartment, pack, arrange movers, etc.) - Executes in sequence

How screens rust executive function: - They do all planning for you - Example: Morrowind (2002) had complex text directions - Modern games: objective markers, quest logs, minimaps - Streaming: autoplay, skip credits, skip intros - TikTok: infinite scroll, algorithm decides what you see

Result: People literally cannot plan. Not dumb — the planning circuit has atrophed.

docs.title: 7. Impulse Control Atrophy
docs.text:
Normal impulse control: - Impulse arises: "I don't feel like studying" - Frontal lobe restrains: "No, we're studying" - Action follows long-term goals

Screens eliminate the need for restraint: - Autoplay next episode - Skip credits automatically - Skip intro button - "Show me more" button - Short-form content requires tiny effort

Platform tactics: - Make scrolling easy (tiny touch) - Make quitting hard ("can't stop on a win/loss") - Bright colors and sounds activate impulses - Everything designed to make you give in

Result: Impulse control muscles atrophy from disuse. When you need to actually resist, the circuit doesn't work.

docs.title: 8. The Multi-Circuit Arms Race
docs.text:
Evolution of game design: 1. Singleplayer RPGs (story) 2. + MMOs (social circuit) 3. + Progression (achievement circuit) 4. + Agency (control circuit) 5. + Mastery (competence circuit) 6. + Community (belonging circuit) 7. + Identity (status/rank circuit)

Platforms compete by activating more circuits: - TikTok, Reels, Shorts activate: dopamine + novelty + visual + (sometimes) social - Each additional circuit makes content exponentially more addictive

docs.title: 9. Clinical Manifestations
docs.text: Dr K observes these problems correlate with screen time: - Lack of willpower - Don't know what to want in life - Not motivated enough - Get bored easily - Can't focus - Social difficulties - "Everyone has ADHD now"

docs.title: 10. Statistics
docs.text:
• Average screen time: 4 hours 37 minutes per day (cell phone only)
  • Heavy users: 6-7 hours daily
  • HG community: Typically exceeds average significantly
  • Note: These numbers exclude other screens (computer, TV)

docs.title: Recovery Strategy
docs.text:
1. Acknowledge the problem: These aren't character flaws — they're screen addiction manifestations
  2. Listen to instinct: Screen use is likely a big part of the problem
  3. Take a break from screens: First and foremost intervention
  4. Nature exposure: Go outside, walk, be in natural environments
  5. Delay screen use: Push first screen interaction as late as possible
  6. Do productive things: Reinforce healthy behaviors to retrain circuits
  7. Be patient: Rebuilding receptors and strengthening frontal lobe takes time

docs.title: Promoted Resources
docs.text:
• Dr K's Guide to Mental Health: Synthesizes monk training and clinical psychiatry experience; covers meditation, ADHD, trauma; 100+ navigable videos; available in YouTube store
  • Free resource packs: Available for those unable to afford full guide

docs.title: Notable Quotes
docs.text:
"These problems of lack of willpower I don't know what I want in life I'm not motivated enough I get bored easily I can't focus oh everyone has ADHD now all of these problems are related to screens"

"The human body doesn't wear out the human body rusts if you don't use your muscles they become flabby if you use them more you will become stronger"

"All these platforms are fighting a war where they are trying to get you to give into your impulses more and more and more"

"Screens do all the planning for you... They break apart all the steps for you so you even remember like when I was playing morrowwind right so a hundred years ago back in the good old days of gaming like there's this Elder Scrolls game called morrowwind it's Elder Scrolls 3 and one of the first quests that you get is like you need to go to suip and punabi and they give you this really complex text about how to find suip and punabi"

"This is what I've seen clinically and we don't we don't even have studies for this stuff because like this stuff is so new we don't even think we're still debating whether video game addiction is a real thing or not"

docs.title: Key Takeaways
docs.text:
1. Terminal boredom is real — it's an endstage manifestation of screen addiction, not laziness or character flaw
  2. Receptor downregulation is the mechanism — your brain eliminates receptors to protect from overstimulation, but this eventually makes everything feel unrewarding
  3. Body rusts, doesn't wear out — lack of use causes atrophy, just as muscles become flabby without exercise
  4. Screens rust executive function — by doing all planning and decision-making for you
  5. Screens atrophy impulse control — by removing the need to restrain impulses
  6. Platforms are in an arms race — each evolution activates more brain circuits, making content more addictive
  7. Recovery is possible but takes time — you need to retrain circuits just as you'd rebuild muscle through exercise

docs.title: Neural Nexus Pages
docs.text:
This video informed the following concepts:

  • terminal-boredom: Endstage manifestation of screen addiction
  • dopamine-tolerance: Receptor downregulation mechanism
  • executive-function-rust: How screens atrophy planning abilities
  • impulse-control-atrophy: How screens weaken restraint mechanisms
  • brain-rot: Content that creates these problems

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Dr K emphasizes this is a new phenomenon — smartphones were invented in 2007, so we've only had ~17 years of widespread smartphone addiction
  • Clinical observations precede research — science is still debating whether video game addiction is real while clinicians see endstage manifestations daily
  • The "rust" metaphor is crucial — these problems are atrophy, not permanent damage. With use (exercise), circuits can strengthen again

docs.title: The Horror of the Zodiac Killer || The Infographics Show
Overview
docs.text: This documentary-style video examines the infamous Zodiac Killer case, one of America's most notorious unsolved murder mysteries. The video explores the crimes, investigation challenges, and cultural impact of this serial killer who terrorized Northern California in the late 1960s and early 1970s.

docs.title: The Zodiac Killer's Reign of Terror
docs.text:
• Active from 1968 to 1972 in Northern California
  • Responsible for at least 5 confirmed murders, with claims of up to 37
  • Known for taunting police and media with cryptic letters
  • Created and sent complex ciphers to authorities

docs.title: Signature Characteristics
docs.text:
• Distinctive crosshair symbol used in communications
  • Mixed methods: shooting, stabbing, and attempted bombing
  • Targeted young couples in isolated areas
  • Pattern of escalating violence and public taunting

docs.title: The Investigation
docs.text:
• Challenged by lack of forensic technology in the era
  • Multiple suspects but no definitive conviction
  • Cryptic messages remain partially unsolved
  • Cold case status with ongoing interest from investigators

docs.title: Cultural Impact
docs.text:
• Inspired numerous books, films, and documentaries
  • Created one of America's most enduring crime mysteries
  • Advanced criminal profiling techniques
  • Demonstrates challenges in solving complex serial crimes

docs.title: Educational Value
docs.text: The video serves as an educational resource for understanding: - Criminal investigation methodologies - The psychology of serial killers - Historical context of cold case investigations - Media's role in criminal cases - The evolution of forensic science

docs.title: The Cipher Mystery
docs.text:
• One of the ciphers was solved in 2020
  • Others remain partially decoded or completely unsolved
  • The killer's identity remains unknown
  • Potential connections to other crimes still being investigated

docs.title: Modern Investigation Efforts
docs.text:
• DNA evidence re-examination
  • Advanced forensic techniques applied to old evidence
  • Public interest and amateur sleuth contributions
  • Potential connections to other cold cases

docs.title: Coffee Intake, Testosterone, and Cardiometabolic Markers (NFBC1966)
docs.text: Authors: Verroest L, Jokelainen J, Choudhary S, Walkowiak J, Karhu T, Palaniswamy S, Auvinen J, Järvelin M-R, Herzig K-H, Raza GS (2026) Journal: European Journal of Nutrition, 65, 215 DOI: 10.1007/s00394-026-04038-z

docs.title: Executive Summary
docs.text:
• In 2,264 adults aged 46 (NFBC1966), higher coffee intake associated with leaner body composition despite similar BMI — lower body fat %, visceral fat, and higher skeletal muscle mass
  • Coffee intake inversely correlated with circulating BCAAs in both sexes — a potentially novel finding relevant to insulin resistance and cardiometabolic risk
  • In men, coffee independently associated with higher total testosterone (+0.29 nmol/L per cup/day), bioavailable testosterone, and SHBG, alongside lower free testosterone and FAI
  • In women, hormonal associations limited to higher SHBG and lower free testosterone/FAI — no total testosterone association
  • Cross-sectional design; causality not established

docs.title: Key Findings
docs.text:
1. Leaner body composition: Higher coffee groups had lower body fat % (p < 0.001), lower fat mass (p = 0.002), lower visceral fat area (p = 0.048), and higher skeletal muscle mass (p < 0.001) — despite comparable BMI across groups

  2. Inverse BCAA correlation: Coffee intake inversely correlated with branched-chain amino acids (isoleucine, leucine, valine) in both men and women. Elevated BCAAs are established predictors of insulin resistance, T2D, and CVD

  3. Favourable glucose-insulin profile (men): Higher coffee intake correlated with lower fasting insulin, lower HOMA2-IR, and higher insulin sensitivity (QUICKI) — only in men

  4. Sex-specific testosterone pattern (men): Fully adjusted models: total testosterone β = +0.29 nmol/L per cup/day (p < 0.001), bioavailable testosterone β = +0.08 (p = 0.003), SHBG β = +0.57 (p < 0.001). Inverse: FAI β = −0.36 (p < 0.001), free testosterone β = −0.01 (p < 0.001)

  5. SHBG pathway (women): Coffee positively associated with SHBG (β = +1.27, p = 0.015) and inversely with FAI (β = −0.32, p = 0.026) and free testosterone (β = −0.01, p = 0.015). No total/bioavailable testosterone associations

  6. Metabolic correlation breadth: Men showed broader metabolomic correlations (alanine, tyrosine, omega-3, glycerol, LDL/IDL fractions) than women (narrower: glycerol, omega-3, leucine, citrate, glutamine, glycine)

  7. BP findings: Systolic BP modestly higher in high coffee consumers (~1.6–3.6 mmHg), but measured after 12h fast/coffee abstention — unlikely acute caffeine effect

docs.title: Clinical Implications
docs.text:
• The concurrent increase in total testosterone + SHBG + decrease in FAI maps onto a hormonally favourable profile — both low total testosterone and low SHBG are independent predictors of MetS and T2D in men
  • SHBG is an independent predictor of T2D risk in both sexes; the coffee-SHBG association may partly mediate coffee's protective effect against T2D
  • Inverse BCAA association may represent a novel metabolic pathway linking coffee to reduced insulin resistance
  • Cross-sectional — cannot establish causality or rule out reverse causation (healthier people drink more coffee)

docs.title: Concepts Covered
docs.text:
• coffee-and-body-composition — leaner profile despite similar BMI
  • coffee-and-bcaa — inverse BCAA correlation, insulin resistance relevance
  • coffee-and-testosterone — sex-specific androgen profile
  • coffee-and-shbg — SHBG as mediator of metabolic protection
  • coffee-and-glucose-metabolism — favourable glucose-insulin in men
  • sex-differences-in-coffee-metabolism — broader metabolic correlations in men
  • caffeine-mechanisms — adenosine antagonism, sympathetic activation, thermogenesis

docs.title: Why "Brain Rot" Content is So Addictive & How to Break Free (YouTube, 32:11)
docs.text: Creator: Dr K (Healthy Gamer) Date: Not specified in transcript Duration: 32:11 Video ID: eu9uvBYsPXs URL: Why Brain Rot is So Addictive

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Dr K explains why "brain rot" content (TikTok, YouTube Shorts, Instagram Reels, rage bait, OnlyFans, etc.) is so addictive and how to break free. The video covers the dopamine lemon metaphor, how modern content hijacks evolutionary circuits, the health consequences of excessive screen time, and practical recovery strategies.

docs.title: 1. The Dopamine Lemon Metaphor
docs.text:
Your brain's dopamine circuitry is like a big lemon full of juice each morning. You have two types of activities:

Activity Type Analogy Effect Pleasurable activities (video games, social media, scrolling) Squeezing the lemon really hard Juice (dopamine) runs out quickly Boring activities (work, chores, paperwork) Squeezing the lemon gently Juice comes out efficiently

The core problem: Once you've emptied the lemon through hard squeezes (high-dopamine activities), you have no dopamine left to reward boring activities. You need to squeeze incredibly hard to get any juice out — but boring activities don't provide enough stimulation to generate that force.

Healthy sequence: Do meaningful work first (gentle squeeze) → get behavioral reinforcement → still have dopamine left for leisure in the evening.

docs.title: 2. Artificial Brain Circuit Activation
docs.text:
Modern content artificially activates survival circuits without providing the evolutionary benefits those circuits evolved for:

Circuit Original Purpose Brain Rot Exploitation Dopamine reward Reinforce survival behaviors (eating, reproducing, socializing) Provide cheap reward without survival benefit Oxytocin release Form social bonds through touch and proximity Parasocial relationships with creators (fake connection) Stress response Prepare for physical action (fight/flight) Rage bait spikes vitals without activity

The calorie vs nutrition problem: Brain rot provides calories without nutrition. Candy bars give energy and pleasure but no actual nutrition → obesity, insulin resistance. Brain rot activates dopamine circuits but no real social connection, accomplishment, or learning → motivation collapse, social atrophy, depression.

Darwinian selection: Platforms algorithmically select the most addictive content. What "rots your brain the most" rises to the top.

docs.title: 3. Rage Bait
docs.text:
Rage bait is content deliberately designed to trigger anger:

  • Physiological effect: Spikes heart rate and blood pressure (similar to exercise)
  • The problem: No physical movement accompanies the spike
  • Result: Cardiovascular damage without the benefit of actual exercise
  • Mechanism: Activates fight/flight circuit but you're sitting still

docs.title: 4. Parasocial Relationships
docs.text:
Parasocial content activates social bonding circuits with fake relationships:

The OnlyFans example: - Fans pay creators for direct messages (DMs) - Transactional: Money → Personalized message - Feels like connection but it's illusory - 45-year-old employee reality: The person on the other end is often not who you think they are

The problem: Brain releases oxytocin (bonding hormone) from fake connections, reducing drive to build real relationships. Real oxytocin comes from real connection; fake oxytocin satisfies the circuit without providing actual social benefit.

Important nuance: Not all online relationships are parasocial. Real human connection can happen online. The problem is when transactional, parasolic interactions replace actual relationships.

docs.title: 5. The Inflammation Cycle
docs.text:
Screen time creates a vicious physiological cycle:

High inflammatory burden → Poor sleep → Low willpower
                                      ↓
Can't resist brain rot → Stay up late consuming content
         ↑                                          ↓
         └─────── Inflammation worsens ←─────────────┘

How it works: 1. High screen time/gaming → elevated IL-6 (immune activation), leptin dysregulation, insulin resistance 2. Inflammation → poor sleep quality 3. Poor sleep → depleted frontal lobe willpower 4. Low willpower → cannot resist brain rot 5. Stay up late consuming content 6. Disrupt sleep further → worse inflammation → repeat

Inflammation is linked to depression, anxiety, and sleep problems. The cycle is self-reinforcing and hard to break.

docs.title: 6. Health Consequences
docs.text:
Research shows concerning correlations between excessive screen time/gaming and:

Cardiovascular: - Blood clots and strokes in 20-somethings (conditions typically seen in 60+) - Increased heart rate, systolic and diastolic blood pressure, ventilation (similar to exercise but without physical benefit)

Metabolic: - Screen time linked to elevated IL-6, leptin dysregulation - Insulin resistance associated with leisure screen time

Immune/Dermatological: - Gaming and mobile phone use worsen eczema and asthma symptoms - Elevated IL-6 linked to autoimmune disease activation

Cognitive/Social: - Atrophy of body language, tone, and eye contact skills - Collapse of motivation to build real relationships - Motivation collapse from fake satisfaction

docs.title: 7. Solutions
docs.text:
Principle: Broccoli Effect Works Both Ways

Just as candy bars kill your craving for broccoli, eating broccoli reduces your desire for candy bars. The same applies to brain rot:

  • Start day with nutritious activities before dopamine-intensive content
  • If dehydrated, drink water → soda craving naturally decreases
  • Engage in real social connection → parasocial content loses appeal

Core Strategy: Build a Life Worth Living

  1. Identify the need: Ask "what am I really getting from this?" (social connection? joy? accomplishment? anxiety relief?)
  2. Find healthier sources: Satisfy those same needs outside brain rot content
  3. Start small: Pick 1-2 activities, do them early in the day
  4. Leverage physiology: Get biology working for you, not against you

Three Pillars of Recovery:

Pillar Action Rationale Nutritious activities 1-2 meaningful activities early in day (work, real social connection, healthy food) Satisfy brain circuits before artificial activation Reduce inflammation Anti-inflammatory diet (2+ servings fruits/vegetables daily), 30 min exercise/day, consider Omega-3/fish oil (consult doctor) Improves sleep, mood, willpower; breaks inflammation cycle Sleep hygiene 7+ hours, no screens 1 hr before bed, Yoga Nidra 1 hr before bed, consider melatonin (consult doctor) Restores frontal lobe willpower; increases resistance to brain rot

Daily Routine Recommendation (Total: ~1 hour/day): - Morning: 1-2 nutritious activities (30 min meaningful work + healthy breakfast) - Midday: 30 min exercise (walk, any movement that activates cardiovascular system) - Evening: Sleep hygiene (no screens, Yoga Nidra 1 hr before bed)

docs.title: Key Takeaways
docs.text:
1. Protect your morning dopamine: Don't squeeze the lemon hard first thing. Front-load boring activities when your brain can still find reward in them.
  2. Brain rot is calories without nutrition: It satisfies reward circuits without providing real benefits, causing "dopamine obesity."
  3. The inflammation cycle is self-reinforcing: High inflammation → poor sleep → low willpower → more brain rot → worse inflammation. Break it with diet, exercise, and sleep.
  4. Broccoli effect works both ways: Eating "nutritious" activities reduces craving for "junk" brain rot. Start the day with 1-2 meaningful things.
  5. Get biology on your side: Anti-inflammatory diet, exercise, and sleep hygiene improve willpower and make recovery easier.
  6. Not all online connection is bad: Real relationships can happen online. The problem is transactional, parasolic substitutes.

  3. "Associations of sedentary behavior and screen time with biomarkers of inflammation and insulin resistance" — Research paper on IL-6, leptin, insulin

docs.title: Autism Spectrum Disorder and IQ – A Complex Interplay
docs.text: Authors: Wolff N, Stroth S, Kamp-Becker I, Roepke S, Roessner V (2022) Journal: Frontiers in Psychiatry, 13, Article 856084 DOI: 10.3389/fpsyt.2022.856084

docs.title: Executive Summary
docs.text:
• ASD heterogeneity is partly determined by IQ differences; the IQ distribution in ASD has shifted over time from majority cognitive impairment to a more balanced distribution
  • Epidemiological vs clinical studies show divergent IQ profiles — clinical samples report more above-average IQ individuals due to referral and sampling biases
  • IQ measurement validity in ASD is compromised by test format demands that overlap with ASD core deficits (social communication, flexibility), creating circularity in diagnostic assessment
  • Bimodal IQ distribution observed in specialized outpatient clinics: ~38% below average (IQ < 85), ~40% above average (IQ > 115), ~22% average

docs.title: Key Findings
docs.text:
1. Historical shift in IQ distribution: Early epidemiological studies (1966–2001) reported 40–100% of ASD individuals with cognitive impairment (IQ < 70, mean 70%). More recent studies show decline to ~31% with IQ < 70, with 44% in average-to-above range.

  2. Epidemiological vs clinical discrepancy: Clinical studies consistently report higher proportions of above-average IQ in ASD compared to epidemiological studies, reflecting referral bias (specialized clinics attract higher-IQ, later-diagnosed individuals).

  3. Bimodal clinical distribution: In specialized ASD outpatient clinics, researchers observed a bimodal IQ distribution — clusters at both low and high IQ extremes, with fewer individuals in the average range.

  4. IQ test validity concerns: Standard IQ tests (e.g., Wechsler scales) require abilities impaired in ASD (verbal comprehension, processing speed, social understanding). This makes IQ scores potentially underestimating true cognitive capacity in ASD.

  5. ADOS-IQ circularity: The Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule (ADOS) is calibrated differently across IQ levels, and IQ influences ADOS scores. This creates reciprocal influence between diagnostic instrument and IQ measure.

  6. Diagnostic delay by IQ level: Higher-IQ individuals receive ASD diagnosis later (often adulthood), while lower-IQ individuals are diagnosed in childhood. This has implications for support access and identity development.

  7. Sample biases identified:

  8. Referral bias: Specialized clinics see more high-IQ ASD individuals
  9. Diagnostic bias: IQ influences who gets diagnosed and when
  10. Reporting bias: Epidemiological studies often collapse above-average IQ data

docs.title: Clinical Implications
docs.text:
• IQ should not be treated as a fixed trait in ASD but as an interacting factor that influences diagnosis, support needs, and outcomes
  • Diagnostic instruments need IQ-stratified norms and awareness of IQ-test overlap with ASD core deficits
  • Later-diagnosed (often higher-IQ) individuals face unique challenges: missed childhood support, identity disruption, comorbid mental health conditions
  • Service provision must account for the full IQ spectrum, not just the cognitive impairment end

challenges actually goes up we have way more passive challenges because we're cutting out things that we want and this actually reinforces the feeling of overwhelmed and this is how we end up getting stuck and so we sort of discovered that the solution to this may seem completely counterintuitive which is to actually increase the number of active challenges in your life and if you're skeptical of that it makes perfect sense because it is counterintuitive but there's actually really good data to back this up and we kind of discovered this principle in the most bizarre place which is with eating disorders and you may start to wonder okay what does that have to do with anything that we're talking about so clinicians made a really interesting observation that the more out of control someone's parts of their life what they do to avoid feeling overwhelmed is to start to really control their eating so they make that challenge of eating so great that it gives them a sense of control in life docs.title: Key Points
docs.text:
• While: While inside, they had intended to steal several important campaign documents and attempted  to plant bugs to listen in on phone lines
  • The: The  Watergate Scandal forever changed US politics, leading many Americans to think more  critically about their leaders – after all, if the President could use his power to attempt to  cover up something like this and get away with it, then it didn’t exactly smack of being trustworthy
  • Still,: Still, one of  the ways that criminals tried to make money during Prohibition was by producing their own illegal  booze to sell on the black market – and can you guess what they stole to use as a key ingredient
  • Hubbard: Hubbard  himself managed to evade facing legal consequences for Operation Snow White; however, he would end up  spending the remainder of his life in hiding from the authorities, considered to be an ‘unindicted  co-conspirator’ for his hand in having members of his cult infiltrating the US government
  • But,: But, indeed, little green or grey men and flying saucers have  long been a mainstay of conspiracy theories

reactive and has a built-in web server so you can browse to it to configure effects and so on it also Sports a remote control so that you can step through the effects and select colors and so on and speaking of colors most every color effect running here in my shop is powered by an esp32 as well the windows you see behind me are running a simple color fill effect and each window has its own esp32 connected to about 800 LEDs that ring the edge of the window of course we can make it much more Dynamic like we can set it the windows to flames but that might be a little distracting during the video so that's why I leave it on solid colors when recording an episode now it would be a lot of pain to try to maintain all of these different effects around the shop much less coordinate or change the effects and have them be consistent between the strips that's when I decided that I was going to add Wi-Fi to the mix now as I mentioned there's an existing package called wed that also has some Wi-Fi support but it's quite different wld uses what's knowing a UDP broadcast and the timing and even success of UDP isn't guaranteed it's basically fire and forget it from the server and you hope your strips all get the signal at about the same time and if they all even get it if they don't it looks terrible night driver takes a slightly more rigorous approach it uses tcpip sockets instead of UDP which means the delivery of each and every packet of color data is guaranteed or at least you'll know both the drop still ensuring that each strip shows the same frame of the same effect at the same time could be challenging so what I wind up doing was sinking the clock in each of the esp32s Via ntp to the atomic clock in Boulder Colorado on each of esp32 there's a circular buffer of frames of color data up to the limit of available memory and each one has a time stamp that indicates when it should be shown when a frame comes due it's immediately showing on the LED strip and as frames are received over Wi-Fi they're added into that circular key Q in this way all of the strips show the exact same frame at the exact same time now a basic esp32 can handle about 30 frames of data in its buffers and at 30 frames per second that means it can survive about a 1C Wi-Fi hiccup but because I wanted a bit more resiliency I bought modules with PS Ram support and then added psram support to night driver and that gives each strip up to about 500 buffers or 15 seconds and if the Wi-Fi is down for more than about 15 seconds it's likely really down but the strips Will Survive more transient issues without any Dropout this ability goes well beyond just keeping two strips in sync though it also enables you to create an LED drawing canvas that spans multiple disconnected strips for example around the perimeter of the shop is an ambient color strip I wanted the colors to be continuous around the ceiling but the cabinets aren't continuous and so I didn't want to fish wires so I added code instead that enabled spanning a single LED strip effect across multiple modules scattered around disconnected physical locations that that means the strips are connected to and take their directions from the same server over Wi-Fi and there's no other connection between them yet they run in reliable perfect sync now even I'll admit that it's a bit of overkill for this ambient strip but the fun doesn't end there there's a guest house out back that features an LED strip that runs for more than 100 ft around its perimeter and it's all 144 LEDs per meter that means there are almost 5,000 LEDs in the strip and they're connected to four different esp32s at the server they're joined to become a big single canvas and then effects are rendered to the whole thing and it just works thanks to night driver my favorite effect is the fireworks effect because the effect spans all four modules virtually particles fly back and forth from strip to strip without interruption and are perfectly timed when they cross strip boundaries you might wonder why I'd go to all the work of adding virtual Wi-Fi support when I could I suppose just Cascade the data wire from LED strip onto the next one right and the problem that arises is the frequency with which you can update the LEDs this data signal is limited to around 30,000 LEDs per second and at 24 bits of color it sounds admirably fast and it actually is but there are still some practical imitations it means you can only do about 1,000 LEDs at once at 30 frames per second and that's why the Cabana fireworks installation must be split across four disconnected strips if it were all one long strip you'd get at most about 6 frames per second and that's just not enough but with synchronized Wi-Fi they draw in parallel and they refresh it once and they run at 30 frames per second and it's all beautiful now the night driver code is all public and completely free open source for non-commercial use under GPL version 3 you can get it at docs.text: TCP vs UDP networking protocols comparison and analysis. This video explains the fundamental differences between Transmission Control Protocol and User Datagram Protocol, including reliability guarantees, connection establishment, error handling, and appropriate use cases for each protocol in modern networking environments. Dave Plummer provides practical examples and demonstrations to help viewers understand when to use TCP versus UDP in different scenarios.

docs.title: Key Points
docs.text:
• More: More importantly, each UDP datagram is an independent message
  • What: What UDP does not contain is just as important
  • Modern: Modern stacks have more sophisticated loss detection, but the core idea remains
  • 9999: 9999 gigabytes very quickly and then a note saying that one critical byte could not be located
  • If: If the most important thing is every byte, then TCP gives you an extraordinarily capable machine for turning an unreliable packet network into something that looks like a reliable stream

they had actually included a bootable micro SD card with the Orin but I didn't see it taped to the side of the box and that means I went through the whole mundane process of downloading the SD card image from nvidia's website fidgeting with the tiniest micro SD card slot that I've ever seen and eventually booting into auntu Linux if there's a golden rule of developer boards this your patience is tested long before your programming skills over are I spent far too long poking around and prodding at the MicroSD Port but once that hurdle was cleared it was smooth sailing fortunately it's not something you have to do very often so otherwise it might be a concern one thing I should mention I added a 1 tbte Samsung 970 Evo SSD to give the oron Nano a bit of breathing room room now during the initial Ubuntu setup it defaulted to installing the operating system on the micro SD card instead of the SSD not ideal after some tinkering I cloned the system from the SD card onto the SSD using Linux command line tools like DD EF CK and resized to FS to make everything fit and with that the system was now booting off the SSD and the performance was definitely night and day in terms of disc it's worth the effort if you're planning to do anything intensive with it I even repeated the setup to confirm that I wasn't given a choice of install Drive which I still find odd now what makes the oron Nano particularly intriguing is its support for nvidia's AI ecosystem including tensor RT Cuda and a host of pre-trained models that makes it a solid candidate for AI enthusiasts like me who might not be ready to train their own GPT model from scratch but still want to dabble in the technology that powers things like Tesla's self-driving cars or Amazon's new Alexa with that in mind I decided to put the or n to work on a simple yet practical AI application a driveway monitor and this isn't your run-of-the-mill beam detect now this is a custom python script that uses a YOLO V8 object detection model to identify Vehicles entering and leaving my driveway the goal to teach the Jetson not just to detect motion but to understand what it's seeing and to notify me accordingly the script is where the magic happens at its core it uses the ultral litic YOLO Library running directly on the GPU to analyze video frames from my security camera feed in real time YOLO or you only look once is an object detection model that true to its name analyze izes an entire frame in a single pass making it extremely fast and speed does matter when you're dealing with live video streams so let's break the script down the script initializes the YOLO model and configures it to run on the oron Nano's GPU this isn't just about speed it's about maximizing this Hardware's potential and here's the kicker YOLO comes pre-trained on a massive data set so right out of the box it already knows how to recognize cars trucks buses and more my job was to narrow its focus to vehicles and tweak confidence thresholds to avoid any false positives after all I don't want it mistaking my dog for a Corvette the script also includes a rudimentary tracking system to keep tabs on individual vehicles I calculate the overlap between deducted bounding boxes to decide whether an object is new or just the same car moving around that way it doesn't show vehicle arriving every time somebody nudges their car forward a few inches and here's the fun part the system doesn't just detect the vehicles it notifies me over the intercom using text to speech modules if a car pulls up it announces vehicle arriving if it leaves I vehicle leaving might seem like a gimmick but it's been surprisingly effective out here in the shop the key is keeping the announcements infrequent enough that they don't turn into background noise in the final setup the script processes video frames at a few frames per second on the Orin but that's fast enough for my purposes and the oron Nano barely breaks a sweat doing it the tracking system also assigns unique IDs to vehicles and keeps a history of their movements over time I could extend this to include more advanced analytics say recognizing specific cars or who might be driving them or alerting when an unknowing vehicle arrives the oron Nano's architecture makes it possible to handle all of this in real time it offloads the heavy lifting like the neural network inference to its caor freeing up the CPU for other tasks it's this seamless interplay between the hardware and the software that sets the Jetson apart from say a Raspberry Pi or similar boards and because it's from Nvidia it works with Cuda and working with Cuda is almost a prerequisite for doing AI these days now let's pivot to a completely different AI use case for the oron Nano butning large language models locally with llama and the Llama 3
  • 2: 2 processing a large language model locally requires not only substantial computational power but also efficient resource allocation the oron Nano's Reliance on its CA cores and six arm CPU cores demonstrated its optimized architecture for AI workloads using all six arm cores for CPU side operations and offloading as much as possible to its Cuda cores the system managed to generate around 21 tokens per second while this might not sound blazing fast as compared to cloud gpus or the high-end desktops it's important to remember that this is a 15w device and it's at least an order of magnitude faster than the pi and then some the verbose output showed steady token generation with the GPU utilization hovering around 60% the story itself was rich and detailed and while the processing time was longer than you'd experience on a high-end workstation the Orin Nano proved as more than capable of running Cutting Edge language models in the end those 20 tokens per second are easily fast enough to make it responsive enough for fluid text to speech answering questions or using the model to solve problems in real time for comparison I ran the same test on an M2 Mac Pro Ultra and it's a fairly maxed out machine as well with the maximum number of GPU cores I think it's 76 in the Mac world and as expected the Mac Go perform the oron Nano by a factor of about five generating tokens at an impressive of 113 tokens per second this performance is largely due to the m2's unified memory architecture and highly efficient neural engine both of which which are optimized for handling AI tasks the significant difference in token generation speeds highlights the disparity and computational power between the two systems but also underscores the efficiency of the Orin Nano given its limitations however what's fascinating is how close the Orin Nano comes given its size and power constraints the Mac Pro represents the Pinnacle of Apple's desktop processing power with its custom silicon optimized for AI tasks it also cost more than $10,000 the oron Nano on the other hand is a $249 developer board designed for Edge Computing despite this it holds its own in a way that's nothing short of remarkable now if you need even more performance out of the system we can go to a more compact version of llama 3

ashes told by somebody who was there Longhorn was supposed to be revolutionary in the early 2000s after the success of Windows XP Microsoft's plan was to follow up with an interim release code named Longhorn before the next major Windows code Nam black home in fact the Coden name Longhorn itself comes from a bar between those two ski mountains Whistler and black home in British col Columbia a nod that longhorn would be a stop gap between Windows and XP or Whistler and the big future OS to be known as blackcomb but as development went on Longhorn grew in scope it started absorbing many ambitious features that originally intended for the future Black Comb release in other words this minor interim release ballooned into a major overhaul of Windows and the goalpost would keep moving so what was the vision well Microsoft wanted Longhorn to reimagine what Windows could be we're talking about very fundamental Chang is under the hood and a flash a completely new user experience on the top one of the crown jewels of this Vision was something called winfs short for Windows future storage the idea behind winfs was to replace or augment the traditional file system known as NTFS with a database driven system the goal was to be able to instantly search and organize all of your files by their content tags relationships and so on not just by file names and folders your documents emails photos and everything would actually live in a database so that fin a file or grouping information would be as easy as querying data it was a bold plan to move beyond the decades old metaphor of files and folders into a richer smarter way of storing information another pillar of LongHorn's Vision was deep integration of Microsoft's new NET Framework into Windows now net was a managed code platform meaning it was a memory safe modern programming model that had debuted in the early 2000s the longhorn team wanted to leverage net to modernize Windows development that meant new apis and sub systems written in managed code instead of the good old C++ win32 all the way for example Longhorn introduced Avalon a code name for the new presentation subsystem essentially a Next Generation graphical user interface framework built onnet Avalon itself would later become known as the windows presentation Foundation there was also Indigo a new Communications and web services framework later known as Windows communication Foundation these were all part of what Microsoft at the time called the Winx Technologies signaling that Longhorns developers were pushing towards manage code and new Frameworks for the future of apps it's not that the windows kernel itself would be Rewritten in C that was never the case or planned but much of the user level infrastructure and apis were planned to get this net based overhaul bringing safer code and quicker development to Windows and we can't forget the user interface dreams Longhorn was slated to entirely revamp the windows UI with a design language village is impressed Perry is considered an important man and the chief allows Perry to marry his daughter the first few months of Perry's married life are pretty good he struggles with malaria but due to his stockpile of army rations he's Rich enough to hire servants to work his Fields Perry spends much of his time hunting monkeys and tigers he grows fluent in his wife's language the couple's excited to find out that they're expecting their first child many nights the tribal musicians play flutes and drums while the tribe chants takes psychoactives and dances meanwhile the Army has offered in Washington DC also his stockpile of rations is quickly dwindling he begins to hunger for Western items especially cigarettes he hires Runners to go down the mountain to trade at the black market in rural towns finally the Army finds a clue in the summer some 5 months after Perry vanished auli finds the rifle Perry accidentally left behind when he panicked at the bridge the Army realizes they've Army brass is incredulous they never would have expected an unarmed Tenderfoot like Perry to survive for so long in the jungle a runner who had gone to the town of namyong to get rice quickly comes back to tell Perry that there are men searching for him Perry leaves his wife in Tuma and goes to noxa or a satellite Village July 20th Captain Walter MCM and a small posy of MPS along with hired Naga guides go on a 3 and a half hour hike up the mountain to Tuma none of the Americans speak any Naga they use a picture of Perry and hand signs to communicate the posi learns that Perry's gone to the agrees which leaves him unarmed Army snipers sneak through the brush and position themselves around Perry's basa they have to be careful it would be diplomatically unwise to accidentally kill any Naga while eating dinner Perry sees flickers of light outside the Naga don't have flashlights it can only mean westerners Perry thinks about trying to sneak into the pitch black jungle behind the village but tigers have recently been appr problem he grabs a DA or short Chinese sword and lights a bamboo staff to use as a torch getting up his nerve Perry goes outside MCM immediately blinds Perry with his body at the bottom of a hill Perry's been shot in the chest around 10: p</li> <li>Mcmin: mcmin hikes several hours back to NY young to get a doctor and more soldiers even with the extra Manpower finally admits his identity and confesses to shooting Katie he's coerced into is signing a three-page document that he's told as a statement of what had happened though Perry thinks some key facts are missing or distorted against his better judgment he notorized and signs the paperwork on August 28th Perry is deemed healthy enough to be transferred to prison he's sent to the notorious Leo stade the very prison he was trying to evade when he shot Katie in the first place this is his second stint in the stade several months before the whole shooting incident Perry had spent hellish months in Leto convicted for disobeying orders when an officer tried to assign him extra work though Perry's sentence for Disobedience was 90 days he'd been forced to serve an extra couple of weeks in The Stockade to tell the Army mainly out of fear of what could happen to them if the Army found out that they had suppressed information about Perry they informed major Earl Owen Cullum commanding officer of the 159th military police Battalion at nearby chowba Camp Cullum decides to set up a trap the soldiers will arrive with the truck and the Army will Ambush Perry tumor and Troxler agree to help as long as the Army's Plan B as he reaches the field MP's fire at Perry but again again he escapes into the jungle this time he's wounded a bullet nicked his right foot he packs it full of moss so it won't get infected a trick he learned from the Naga Perry limps through the jungle and hides in a rice Patty hours later he awakes to The Barking of German Shepherds the Army's caught up to him Perry escapes capture Perry February February 22nd A desperate Perry hides by the side of the Leo Road his new plan is to board a truck hide among the supplies and hit a ride over the mountains when the truck reaches Burma he'll ditch it and disappear into the jungle but Perry is unwell The Gunshot on his foot is very painful also he's had to drink river water and has caught dissenter when Perry tries to coordinates with a British and Native police forces he and his fellow posi follow Perry's Trail for over 2 weeks Cullum eventually figures out that Perry's headed in the direction of the town of namrup Perry's following the Southeastern branch of the dang River it's a long indirect route to Tunga how however Perry's probably taking this way because just south of dup is considered the gateway
